observations: Freeport reports water only at FCX-global and regional/segment level (Copper Mining North America / South America / Indonesia, Molybdenum Mining, Smelting & Refining North America / Europe, Other) for 2018-2022; there are no individual mine-level water volumes. Indonesia copper mining = PT-FI (Grasberg). South America = Cerro Verde + El Abra. Water supply risk (baseline water stress) is given per operation (Water!A78:F126): Cerro Verde High, El Abra Extremely High; Henderson, Miami, Morenci, Safford, Sierrita Med-High; Bagdad, Chino, Climax, Tyrone Low-Med; PT-FI Low.

Units: thousand cubic metres (= ML, factor 1). Withdrawal is "new water withdrawn" and excludes water diverted without use. Stormwater is reported as its own source (mapped to withdrawal_rain_runoff). Third-party water is primarily wastewater effluent.

Recycling dominates: total recycled/reused 1,526,886 ML vs 291,682 ML new withdrawals in 2022 (reuse rate 83.96%). Recycled volumes rose from 1,231,053 ML (2020) to 1,526,886 ML (2022) while new withdrawals stayed between 261,299 and 310,620 ML.

Trend: new water withdrawals 310,620 ML (2018) -> 302,564 (2019) -> 261,299 (2020, COVID/lower activity) -> 296,805 (2021) -> 291,682 (2022). Seawater withdrawal (all Atlantic Copper, Europe) fell from 49,218 (2020) to 34,719 ML (2022). Europe smelting recycle rate collapsed from 23.8% (2018) to 5.7% (2022).

Discharge concentration: 2022 footnote (Water!A59) says ~36% of discharge is Atlantic Copper estuarine cooling water, 51% PT-FI controlled riverine tailings management system, 12% Climax/Henderson. North America and South America copper mining report zero discharge (except 190.51 thousand m3 in NA 2021). Low-quality discharge to sea/estuary 70,927 thousand m3 in 2022 (PT-FI alkaline tailings water + saline estuarine water).

Indonesia (PT-FI) consumption is very small relative to withdrawal (4,216 of 54,188 ML in 2022) because most water leaves via the riverine tailings system (discharge 49,966 ML). PT-FI change in storage was large in 2018-2019 (16,961 and 12,567 ML) then near zero.

Data inconsistency: in "Water - by region" the Indonesia 2021 recycle/reuse rate (G42 = 64.96) and water-use efficiency (G43 = 96.44) are stored as percentages whereas all other cells store fractions (e.g. H42 = 0.6865); values were used as-is (not multiplied) and flagged in the record note.
Minor rounding inconsistencies within the 2022 tables: total new water withdrawn 291,681.89 (Water!F10) vs 291,681.93 (Water!D34); consumption 197,982.58 (F14) vs 197,982.571 (D43).

Only 2022 has the ICMM high/low quality split: 237,377 thousand m3 high-quality (freshwater) and 54,305 low-quality withdrawal. SASB (SASB!F12): 25% of freshwater withdrawn and 43% of freshwater consumed (128,253 thousand m3) are in High/Extremely High baseline water stress regions. GRI index says FCX does not break withdrawal/discharge/consumption down by water-stress area.

Compliance: environmental penalties US$0 (2018), 124,682 (2019), 67,100 (2020), 18,951 (2021), 24,301 (2022). Water-related: 2021 penalty at El Abra for delays commissioning a real-time groundwater monitoring system; 2022 US$12,959 at Cerro Verde (water discharge monitoring/reporting NOV) and US$1,500 at El Paso refinery (two wastewater discharge permit NOVs). SASB: no water-quality non-compliance resulted in formal enforcement in 2022. One significant environmental event in 2022 at El Abra. NOVs rose from 5 (2019) to 12 (2022).

Production: only 2022 consolidated mine production is stated (SASB!F38): 1,909,624 t copper, 1,811 thousand oz gold, 38,555 t molybdenum; no ore-processed or site-level production in the workbook. Energy/GHG sheets are site-level but have no water data.
Regional withdrawal blocks (copper mining total + molybdenum + smelting & refining total + other) sum to FCX Global in every year 2018-2022.
